[1/4] Plan harden TaskStore root level: reject duplicate task ids, require next_id >= 1, preserve unknown root keys; M2 guards+tests, M3 root-extras round-trip+test, M4 ADR-006+map+gates+commit

impact_assessment.why: Probe analysis of the last two pushes found three gaps in the store contract proven by runtime probes: duplicate ids load silently and break stable-reference behaviour, nonsense next_id values are laundered instead of failing loud, and unknown root keys are deleted on the first write - an asymmetry with the per-task unknown-field preservation ADR-004 established.
impact_assessment.benefits: Malformed or hostile stores fail as the documented RuntimeError before mutation; future store versions keep root-level metadata across writes, matching the round-trip promise already made for task fields.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: two more store shapes now fail loud (duplicate ids, next_id < 1) and one write shape changes (unknown root keys round-trip); a store a future client wrote could carry root keys this client must not drop; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: single-writer unchanged, no locking in scope; state: store files only, no rename of existing keys; members of seen-set ordering matter for the extras map
impact_assessment.mitigation: Three tiny isolated guards plus mirroring the existing per-task extras mechanism for the root; one failure-mode test per guard; ADR-006 records the contract change; full gate suite and strict check before delivery; explicit staging

impact_assessment.risks: contract: two new loud failures and one write-shape change, all recorded in ADR-006; dependency: none; concurrency: unchanged single-writer; state: store files and decisions.md only
impact_assessment.mitigation: Per-guard regression tests including subTest for 0 and -7; full gate suite; explicit staging of the five changed files

[1/4] Plan store durability: save keeps a .bak of the previous store (pre-replace), retries os.replace up to 5 times with injectable delay, best-effort directory fsync; load falls back to .bak when the main file is missing; M2 implement, M3 tests+README+ADR-007 (advisory locking recorded as deferred with single-writer rationale), M4 gates+commit

impact_assessment.why: PRINCIPLE-013 calls for temp+fsync+replace with retries, dir fsync and a .bak for state files; probing confirmed save has none of the three, so a crash mid-save or a rename lost to a stale Windows handle loses the store head, and today the failure leaves no recovery copy.
impact_assessment.benefits: Every save leaves the previous store recoverable as .bak; transient replace failures self-heal; the rename reaches the directory entry unless the platform forbids opening it.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new .bak files appear next to the store and load() reads .bak when the main file is missing (recovery semantics must be documented); dependency: time and os only, standard library; concurrency: no advisory locking yet, deliberate ADR deferral - a lost-update window between load and save remains; state: save failure paths change, temp-file cleanup preserved; if the backup move crashes before the replace lands the main file is absent until the next save, so the fallback load is part of the contract
impact_assessment.mitigation: Recovery semantics and the locking deferral both land in ADR-007; injectable retry delay keeps unit tests under the 20ms budget; per-behaviour regression tests including a mocked transient replace failure; full gates and strict check before delivery; explicit staging

checkpoints.description: [2/4]-[4/4] Implemented and verified: save keeps .bak of previous store, retries replace (5 tries, injectable flat delay), POSIX dir fsync skipped on Windows with hygiene: allow marker; load falls back to .bak; 47 tests pass (3 new); ADR-007 records the locking deferral; README documents recovery; checklists passed

impact_assessment.why: PRINCIPLE-013 durability pattern was absent from the store; a mid-save crash or blocked rename could lose the store head irrecoverably
impact_assessment.benefits: Previous store always recoverable as .bak; transient replace failures self-heal; rename reaches the directory entry on POSIX
impact_assessment.risks: contract: .bak files appear beside the store and missing main files read from .bak; dependency: time module only; concurrency: locking deliberately deferred via ADR-007 single-writer stance; state: save failure paths restructured, temp cleanup preserved
impact_assessment.mitigation: Three regression tests including mocked transient double-failure; retry delay injectable keeping tests fast; ADR-007 and README document the recovery and Windows skip; full gates plus strict check before delivery

[1/4] Plan resolve ADR-004 due-format deferral: one canonical acceptance set for due values; compact YYYYMMDD accepted and canonicalized to YYYY-MM-DD at CLI add/edit and store load; week dates and other parseable-but-non-canonical forms fail loud on every supported runtime; M2 implement canonical_due + validate_due/load wiring, M3 tests + ADR-008 + README wording, M4 gates + commit

impact_assessment.why: ADR-004 deferred strict due parsing because date.fromisoformat accepts non-canonical forms on 3.11+ only, so the same store read differently across the runtimes the README supports; canonicalizing at every entry point converges the accepted set without breaking stores a 3.11 runtime already wrote
impact_assessment.benefits: Due values are comparable and filterable identically on 3.10 and 3.11+; stores self-heal to canonical form on the next write; the open migration question from ADR-004 closes
impact_assessment.risks: contract: due acceptance changes (new compact form accepted, week dates now rejected everywhere) and error message set changes; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: single-writer unchanged; state: due values already stored in non-canonical ISO forms are canonicalized on first write - a one-time normalizing write
impact_assessment.mitigation: canonical_due shared by both entry points (single implementation); per-shape regression tests including week-date rejection and load canonicalization; ADR-008 + README document the acceptance set; full gates and strict check before delivery; explicit staging

[1/3] Plan store schema_version: save writes root schema_version 2; load accepts missing (legacy), requires positive int, refuses newer with a clear error; key lives next to tasks/next_id and is never merged into root extras; ADR-009 records it as the anchor for future migrations; M2 implement, M3 tests+ADR+README, M4 gates+commit

impact_assessment.why: Every store contract change so far (next_id, root extras, canonical due) had to argue from absence of a version marker; a schema_version root key is the smallest durable anchor that lets a future reader detect a newer store before misreading its shape
impact_assessment.benefits: Newer-store protection with an actionable error; explicit format identifier for migration tooling; zero migration needed today
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new root key appears in every save and unknown-version stores now fail load (new guard, previously they loaded blindly); dependency: stdlib; concurrency: single-writer; state: stores this version wrote stay readable (missing key accepted); root extras exclusion grows by one key
impact_assessment.mitigation: guard rejects only strictly-greater versions and non-integer/too-low values as corrupt; backward-compat and newer-store tests; ADR-009; README mentions the schema key; full gates
